title.rendered: 2025 Ken Coleman Extra Mile Award Winners

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Elyse Pleickhardt

Congratulations to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Trustee Liz Rappaport and Tom Mathes, recipients of the 2025 Ken Coleman Extra Mile Award. This coveted award is given to Jimmy Fund volunteers who go above and beyond with their time and efforts in support of Dana-Farber. Liz and Tom have committed decades of their lives to the Jimmy Fund as volunteers at Jimmy Fund Golf and community events, most recently as co-chairs of the Jimmy Fund WMass Classic. Their leadership and steadfast commitment to cancer research and care have helped raise millions over the years.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Caitlin Roberts
Photography by Sam Ogden

Each day at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, faculty members work toward research breakthroughs, provide care and moments of hope to patients, and strive to go above and beyond in the fight against cancer.

Jenny Mack, MD, MPH, faculty vice president for the Office of Faculty Development (OFD) and professor of pediatrics, sees it every day in her role—and has experienced it as a long-time faculty member.

“Whether they are caring for patients or conducting research that can change the face of cancer care, there are so many ways that faculty members help shape the endeavors of Dana-Farber,” shared Mack. “Our donors see that and understand that investing in our faculty means investing in Dana-Farber.”

Philanthropic support helps propel this work forward. Created in 2008, the OFD strives to support career development, build community, aid faculty members during critical moments in their personal lives, and ensure that Dana-Farber is a place they can thrive. Thanks to continuous support totaling more than $2 million, the OFD has provided awards to faculty members across Dana-Farber in a variety of disciplines. This generosity ensures that faculty can deliver the best in research and care for patients, while also flourishing at Dana-Farber, especially those beginning their careers. In fact, many who were supported early in their careers hold leadership positions at Dana-Farber today.

“Supporting early career faculty members can help them for many years, creating avenues to access grants, launch projects, and providing them opportunities that can be more difficult to come by early in their careers. This support can have a ripple effect for faculty members as they move forward, creating long-term success,” said Mack. Generosity toward the OFD helps aid in patient care, too. “By supporting the OFD, donors are supporting the great things faculty members do, including doing their best for patients, both here at Dana-Farber and around the world as scientific discoveries are disseminated across the globe,” commented Mack.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Elyse Pleickhardt
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

On Oct. 6, 2025, Jimmy Fund Co-Chairs Tom Caron and Brock Holt hosted the inaugural Jimmy Fund Pro-Am Golf Tournament at the Tournament Players Club (TPC) Boston. Paired with Boston sports legends, golfers teed off for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and successfully raised funds that support critical cancer care and research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Meet the new Co-Chairs of the Jimmy Fund: Brock Holt and Tom Caron
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Holt and Caron will be the lead ambassadors and public spokespeople on behalf of the Jimmy Fund, helping to raise funds and awareness.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: An un-fore-gettable year with Jimmy Fund Golf
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun raised $6.8 million in 2024, thanks to organizers and participants in more than 140 events across the country.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation honored with the Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Expect Miracles Foundation (EMF) received the 2025 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—during a special on-field ceremony at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Group photo of Jimmy Fund Award winners and Dana-Farber staff at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Golf community helps to usher in the Jimmy Fund’s 75th
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun marked another ace year in 2023, with an array of dedicated tournament directors, sponsors, and supporters across the country raising more than $6.8 million for The Dana-Farber Campaign.

title.rendered: Pan-Mass Challenge is moving to Worcester

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Michael Ivins/Holy Cross

The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), which has raised $1.125 billion for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute since 1980, is relocating its starting line and hub site from Sturbridge to Worcester. The annual bike-a-thon will begin July 31 at the College of the Holy Cross, a site that can accommodate more riders and offer them a new route for the first 23 miles of the ride to Bourne.

“This new partnership with Holy Cross offers our PMC community more space and resources to increase our impact in the fight against cancer,” said PMC Founder and Chairman and Dana-Farber Trustee Billy Starr. One hundred percent of every rider-raised dollar goes directly to cancer research and care at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge makes record-breaking $78 million gift to drive Dana-Farber’s progress against cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), a bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the world, has built an unparalleled track record for success strengthened by touchstone traditions and continuous improvements in pursuit of the goal of defying cancer.

img.alt_text: A child holding a 'We love PMC riders' sign among a group of bike riders

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved is a gravel bike ride over the scenic backroads of the Berkshires in western Massachusetts that raises funds for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: A group of bicycle riders riding along a wooded path

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved riders contributed $1.2 million to the Pan-Mass Challenge's record-breaking gift of $75 million in 2024.

img.alt_text: Bicycle riders on an unpaved path in the woods

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

Spring 2026
By Tarice Gray
Photography by Fergie Medar

The Red Sox brought some welcome warmth and inspiration to the pediatric cancer patients at the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. It was part of their journey of good cheer through the 2025 Holiday Caravan and the visitors included Red Sox players Connor Wong, Connelly Early, Nate Eaton, Nick Sogard, and Payton Tolle. 

The hope-filled meet and greet provided lasting memories for the cancer patients and their families. It was another example of the tremendous support Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund receive from the Red Sox organization throughout the year.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026

Last March 2025, the Massachusetts Public Health Council voted unanimously to approve a Determination of Need (DON) for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to build a 300-bed cancer hospital in the Longwood Medical Area. This approval was a key milestone in the regulatory process that will enable Dana-Farber to build a visionary new inpatient facility that will redefine how cancer is treated.

Dana-Farber is renowned for its revolutionary, groundbreaking research and expert, highly specialized patient care. The hospital will function as the primary connector at the center of the clinical collaboration between Dana-Farber, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC), and Harvard Medical Faculty Physicians (HMFP). It will be the only hospital of its kind in the region. The future cancer hospital has a community of supporters that is building momentum—fueling this next chapter of innovative treatment and care for patients and families. More stories of their commitment to our bold vision for the future of cancer care will be featured in future issues of Impact.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026

Dear Friends,

As the year unfolds and progress accelerates, I am grateful for the passion and generosity of our donor community. Together, we have built tremendous momentum and are transforming cancer research and care. Your continued belief in Dana-Farber’s mission is laying the foundation for the future cancer hospital, a once-in-a-generation effort to expand world-class care and accelerate discovery for the patients and families who count on us.

Dana-Farber’s unique 50-50 model—equal commitment to cancer research and patient care—powers a virtuous cycle: breakthroughs in the lab rapidly inform clinical care and insights from the clinic spark new scientific questions. This integrated approach isn’t just a philosophy; it is a proven engine for progress.

Our commitment to research is unwavering—and growing. The future cancer hospital will strengthen our 50-50 model by creating more opportunities for collaboration, expanding access to clinical trials, and elevating the standard of care for every patient. Philanthropic leaders are providing targeted support for the future cancer hospital, enabling us to sustain and expand strategic research initiatives. This proactive approach deepens discovery, expands clinical care through a clear growth plan, and engages a broader community of supporters to amplify impact.

A landmark grant from the Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation, featured in this issue, exemplifies continued investment in the bench-to-bedside-to-bench continuum in metastatic breast cancer. Their commitment will accelerate clinical trials, sharpen data and liquid biopsy insights, and apply AI to personalize care and anticipate resistance, so that the right therapies reach patients faster.

Because of the Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation and a community of donors that span the globe, we are strengthening the ecosystem that has made and will continue to make Dana-Farber distinct—where science and care continuously inform each other, and where every gift brings us closer to a world free from the burden of cancer. Thank you for believing in this vision and for helping us build a better future for every patient. 

With heartfelt appreciation,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: September has arrived, and with it the end of summer and the close of another successful Jimmy Fund event season.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As I reflect on this past year, I am filled with immense gratitude for the generosity and unwavering commitment of our Dana-Farber community. Your steadfast support has been a driving force behind so many of our achievements, and it is because of you that we have been able to navigate…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Johnston gift paves the way for a novel ovarian cancer clinical trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Debbie Johnston is dedicated to supporting causes that are close to her heart, and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s ovarian cancer research is one such cause.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Zakim Center turns 25: Donor generosity continues to fuel integrative therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the late Leonard “Lenny” Zakim was being treated for multiple myeloma in the 1990s, he found that complementary therapies such as acupuncture, massage, and Tai Chi eased the side effects of chemotherapy and radiation.

img.alt_text: Five members of the Zakim family

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Your generosity on GivingTuesday is fueling the next victory over cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2012, GivingTuesday was created with one simple goal: encourage generosity and collective giving. What was once a small experiment in communal impact is now a worldwide movement comprised of donors who support causes close to their hearts.

img.alt_text: Pediatric patient wearing a pink tutu

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Casey Repasy

A Chance for Kids & Families raised $462,102 in 2025 for cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Throughout the summer, patrons who donated to the Jimmy Fund at participating Burger King®, The Paper Store®, Uncharted, and Valvoline Instant Oil ChangeSM locations received a coupon, with all proceeds supporting Dana-Farber’s lifesaving mission.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Chance for Kids & Families
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A Chance for Kids & Families raised over $425,000 in 2024 for cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber. Patrons who donate to the Jimmy Fund at participating Burger King, The Paper Store, and Valvoline Instant Oil Change locations receive coupons, with all proceeds supporting Dana-Farber’s lifesaving mission.

img.alt_text: A Chance for Kids & Families logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises over $760,000 for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This spring, New England Stop & Shop customers donated over $760,000 to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber through the grocery chain’s annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PopStroke
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised $230,000 to support innovative cancer research and compassionate patient care at Dana-Farber. Thanks to donor support, Dana-Farber patients and their families were able to participate in this unforgettable experience and take the field at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: New England Stop & Shop customers donated $1.4 million to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber last year during the grocery chain’s 31st annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign, which has raised a total of $77 million for the Institute since 1991.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Lucy McDonald

Joel and Mary Abramson pledged $200,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Program for Older Adults with Breast Cancer, led by Rachel Freedman, MD, MPH. Their support will expand this unique, individualized care model, which delivers tailored treatments and psychosocial services that elevate care and expand the access for older patients with breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Advancing equity tops agenda at Women’s Leadership Breakfast
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: More than 220 business and community leaders attended the Women’s Leadership Breakfast hosted by the Executive Council of the Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber faculty and staff speakers at the Women’s Leadership Breakfast hosted by the Executive Council of the Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers

jetpack-related-posts.title: Husband honors late wife with gift to support older breast cancer patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the last essay she would write for her college reunion book, Virginia Aisner quoted one of her favorite lines from Vergil’s Aeneid: “Perhaps, at some time, we shall be glad to remember even these things.”

img.alt_text: A closeup shot of Virginia Aisner

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Barbara Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

Spring 2026
By Casey Repasy

Since 2023, the annual Ang’s Warrior Walk has raised $100,000 for the Angela Marotta Inho Memorial Fund, which supports lung cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Organized by Jennifer and Allison Inho, Founders of the Angela Marotta Inho Foundation, the event honors their mother Angela, who received care at  Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Coughlin Crew
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Michael Coughlin Lung Cancer Research Fund, established in memory of Michael Coughlin, recently surpassed $100,000 in funds generated in support of thoracic oncology at Dana-Farber. The majority of these funds were raised through the family’s Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk team, Coughlin Crew, which first participated in the event…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joe Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly gave $100,000 to fund critical small cell lung cancer research at Dana-Farber. Established in honor of Connolly’s late wife, the Deborah A. Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joe Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly established the Deborah Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund at Dana-Farber in honor of his late wife, with a gift of $100,000. The fund will support research such as studies of the molecular mutations driving small cell lung cancer, with the goal of developing targeted therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Free ME from Lung Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund doubled its impact, matching a previous gift of $100,000 to support research conducted by Jia Luo, MD, in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. The investment will fuel immunotherapy research for patients with an aggressive and underfunded type of lung cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Barbara and Arnold Barron gave $100,000 to support lung cancer research under the direction of Michael Rabin, MD. The couple has supported the work of Rabin and Dana-Farber for many years, this gift marking their latest commitment to spur advancements in durable treatments for lung cancer patients at Dana-Farber and…

Spring 2026
By Caitlin Roberts
Photography by Matt Teuten

The Arbella Insurance Foundation continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through its Strike Out Cancer Program. At the 2025 WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon, the team presented a check for $100,000, part of the more than $1.7 million the Arbella Insurance Foundation has contributed to date.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Milestone 20th annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon raises $3.5 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1953, the Boston Red Sox have had a deep and multifaceted impact on patients with cancer through its strong partnership with Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber patient and doctor on the field at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Special thanks to our friends at Arbella Insurance Foundation, which is making a $50 contribution for each strikeout thrown by a Boston Red Sox pitcher up to $100,000 in total. This promotion has raised more than $1.1 million since 2014 while amplifying Arbella Insurance’s impact as a longstanding Dana-Farber supporter…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

img.alt_text: A group of people holding an over-sized check at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon surpasses $70 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to thousands of generous supporters from across the country, the 21st annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance raised more than $4 million.

img.alt_text: A participant in the Jimmy Fund Radio Telethon

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Another home run year for the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance helped strike out cancer for the 22nd year at Fenway Park in August, raising nearly $4 million for adult and pediatric cancer care and research at Dana-Farber.

Spring 2026
By Hannah White Hannah

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers  Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for patients worldwide.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael Swidler
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received a gracious contribution from Michael Swidler to establish the Nancy Swidler Fund for Breast Cancer Research in honor of his late wife. Managed by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, this fund is intended to advance pioneering breast cancer research and create pathways to better outcomes for every…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joe Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly gave $100,000 to fund critical small cell lung cancer research at Dana-Farber. Established in honor of Connolly’s late wife, the Deborah A. Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joe Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly established the Deborah Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund at Dana-Farber in honor of his late wife, with a gift of $100,000. The fund will support research such as studies of the molecular mutations driving small cell lung cancer, with the goal of developing targeted therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jonathan Mehlman
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jonathan Mehlman gave $100,000, honoring his late wife Marla, in support of breast cancer research under the direction of Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH. With this funding, Tolaney and her team will continue developing new clinical approaches for the most aggressive forms of breast cancer.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Hannah White Hannah

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc, received a $220,000 Early Investigator Award from CURE Childhood Cancer. This generous grant supports her research focused on determining whether targeting two proteins can effectively treat a specific type of acute myeloid leukemia. The grant also helps launch her career as an independent investigator.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Charles H. Hood Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Charles H. Hood Foundation awarded Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc, a generous $200,000 grant to study a combination treatment for acute myeloid leukemia targeting oncogenic fusion proteins and foster her career development as an independent investigator. This funding supports high-risk, high-reward pediatric studies, enabling groundbreaking discoveries, improved care, and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lymphoma Research Foundation awarded Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's Tianfang Ma, PhD, a generous $195,000 Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant, to bolster his research and growth as an independent investigator. Ma’s work focuses on the tumor immune microenvironment in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and may help enhance immunotherapy effectiveness and identify predictive markers…

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation spurs pivotal research aimed at new epigenetic therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is spurring Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s efforts to eradicate difficult-to-treat cancers through recent grants totaling $1.6 million awarded to two Dana-Farber investigators who aim to develop novel treatments known as epigenetic therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber faculty are part of “grand challenge” to defeat childhood tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has been awarded more than $3 million in funding as part of a Cancer Grand Challenge to find new treatments for solid tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation grants millions to advance childhood cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It all began over 20 years ago with a simple, yet profound, act of kindness by Alex Scott, a determined little girl with cancer, who held a lemonade stand fundraiser to help other kids like her and inspired countless others to do the same.

Spring 2026
By Brendan Monihan

Dordick Trial College, an annual legal education event held in May 2025 and organized by attorney Gary Dordick, raised more than $140,000 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. The multiday program convened legal professionals for workshops and networking, with proceeds benefiting critical research and care for patients and families impacted by this disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dordick Trial College surpasses $1 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The event offers trial lawyers and law firms a unique opportunity to network and learn from industry leaders while helping to combat Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia.

img.alt_text: A crowd inside a conference center during a presentation

jetpack-related-posts.title: Fred and Michele Brettschneider
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Fred and Michele Brettschneider made a commitment of $250,000 to support a clinical trial network for Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia and advance all clinical research for this rare form of blood cancer within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Luigi and Patrizia D’Amato
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Luigi and Patrizia D’Amato made a gift of $100,000 to support research within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia at Dana-Farber. The center is the largest in the world dedicated to the study of Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a slow-growing type of blood cancer that most often forms in the bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: IWMF awards $1.4 million to Dana-Farber investigators, fueling Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than two decades, the International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) has been a vital philanthropic partner to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, accelerating research into Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinemia (WM), a rare, slow-growing blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New multi-institution network to drive progress in rare blood cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) recently committed $2.5 million to support a new multi-institutional network for clinical and research programs dedicated to Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM).

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert Cummins
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert Cummins gave $100,000 to establish The Deborah Cummins Waldenström’s Memorial Fund in honor of his late wife. Cummins’ investment is enabling a team at Dana-Farber’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia to lead clinical trials that are pivotal in the development of more durable, effective treatments.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Hannah White Hannah

Mary and John Fowler’s initial gift establishes the John and Mary Fowler Fund for Lynch Syndrome Research, under the direction of principal investigator Matthew B. Yurgelun, MD, FASCO, CGAF. The gift will strengthen the Lynch Syndrome Center’s registry and biobank and accelerate research that will help identify personalized screening, treatment, and prevention strategies for Lynch syndromedriven cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Whittaker Family Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Stephani Batchelor and Andrew Robert Whittaker made an additional gift of $225,000 to Dana-Farber’s Lynch Syndrome Center. This gift supports the leadership of Sapna Syngal, MD, MPH, and Matthew Yurgelun, MD, FASCO, CGAF, and their team in diagnosing Lynch syndrome and advancing screenings, treatments, and prevention strategies to help patients…

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stephanie and Austin Dobson
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With gifts totaling $115,000, Stephanie and Austin Dobson established a family fund in support of Lynch syndrome research led by Sapna Syngal, MD, and Matthew Yurgelun, MD. This fund has already garnered meaningful support from Stephanie’s parents, Paul and Bettina Henderson, as well as generous contributions from supporters of Austin’s…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hooley gift to Lynch Syndrome Center boosts prevention and intervention
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Linda and Jay Hooley of Hingham, Mass., want to change that. They made a $1 million gift to Dana-Farber’s Lynch Syndrome Center.

img.alt_text: A couple pose for a photo in front of water

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sweet family endows first-ever fellowship in Lynch syndrome
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their gifts to Dana-Farber, David and JoEllen Sweet hope to alleviate the burden of Lynch syndrome for future generations.

img.alt_text: Two people pose for a photo with a stone sculpture

jetpack-related-posts.title: John Cassidy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Cassidy’s generous $300,000 gift establishes the Cassidy Family Melanoma Fellowship, to significantly advance melanoma research. Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lori and David Scragg
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Lori and David Scragg made a gift of $300,000 to support the Lynch Syndrome Center at Dana-Farber, a comprehensive multidisciplinary cancer genetics group that specializes in coordinating the care of people with Lynch syndrome, a genetic condition linked to cancer that affects about 1 in 300 people in the U.S.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Tarice Gray

Clinical trials are considered essential for groundbreaking research. To help advance Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s clinical trials, Micki and Steven Hirsch made a gift of $100,000 to the Hirsch Family Fund for the Office of Clinical Research. Jeffrey Meyerhardt, MD, MPH, FASCO, leads the program which has benefited from the generous support of the Hirsch fund since 2019.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Johnston gift paves the way for a novel ovarian cancer clinical trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Debbie Johnston is dedicated to supporting causes that are close to her heart, and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s ovarian cancer research is one such cause.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Richard and Eileen Greisch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Richard and Eileen Greisch made a gift of $100,000 to provide essential resources for melanoma research under the direction of Tamara Sussman, MD. These funds will enable researchers to test novel therapeutics in clinical trials, lead investigations in genomic sequencing, and develop groundbreaking immunotherapeutic approaches.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Levy gift supports Dana-Farber’s vision for the future of cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Sarah Salter Levy and Steven Levy learned of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s plans to build New England’s first inpatient hospital dedicated to adults with cancer, they wanted to be among the first to step forward with philanthropic support.

img.alt_text: Sarah Salter Levy and Steven Levy

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grateful parents fuel clinical trials
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Donor support empowers Dana-Farber to change the lives of patients everywhere. And when a drug developed at the Institute saved a brave girl on the other side of the country, her parents wanted to help Dana-Farber do the same for other children.

img.alt_text: A family posing for a photo in front of a sunset

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Our historic partner, the Dana Foundation, made a new $100,000 commitment to the Defy Cancer Fund, which provides unrestricted support for The Dana-Farber Campaign. These flexible funds propel innovative early stage research, speed new drugs into clinical trials, retain and attract top talent; meet unanticipated needs; and ensure that we…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cox Family continues support of Dana-Farber’s revolutionary science
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Career venture capitalist and Institute Trustee Howard Cox and his wife, Wendy Cox, are no strangers to the revolutionary science and clinical treatments happening at the Institute.

Spring 2026
By Tarice Gray

The IBC Network Foundation made a generous $100,000 gift to advance the inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) research of Filipa Lynce, MD, FASCO. With this, Lynce will explore the ability of T-cell receptors to predict response to immunotherapy and drive progress in the treatment of IBC, which will ultimately offer hope to patients with this rare disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquer Cancer® grants target several types of cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Conquer Cancer®, the ASCO Foundation, has fueled groundbreaking research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute for decades.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Freedlander bequest focuses on inflammatory breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The estate of Ruth Freedlander made a $1.8 million bequest to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that will advance research into inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), a rare and aggressive disease that is particularly difficult to treat.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Micki and Steven Hirsch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Clinical trials are considered essential for groundbreaking research. To help advance Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s clinical trials, Micki and Steven Hirsch made a gift of $100,000 to the Hirsch Family Fund for the Office of Clinical Research. Jeffrey Meyerhardt, MD, MPH, FASCO, leads the program which has benefited from the generous…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen strengthens commitment to breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, Komen reaffirmed its dedication to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute by awarding three new Career Transition Awards totaling $1.95 million, alongside 12 active research grants. This investment underscores Komen's ongoing support for groundbreaking studies and improving outcomes for those affected by breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation continues support with nearly $4 million in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding by the late Evelyn Lauder alongside her dear friend Larry Norton, MD, in 1993, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF) has championed research as the key to one day curing breast cancer.

Spring 2026
By Hannah White Hannah

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Mohammad Rashidian, PhD, received a $250,000 Translational Research Award from the International Myeloma Society and the Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation. This support will advance his innovative work to combat disease relapse in multiple myeloma patients following CAR T-cell therapy.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Mohammad Rashidian, PhD, received The International Myeloma Society and Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation Translational Research Award. He will use his $250,000 grant to empower investigations to address the challenge of disease relapse in patients treated with a specific type of CAR T-cell therapy. Such studies hold great promise in…

jetpack-related-posts.title: IMS grants drive innovative multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Myeloma Society (IMS) recently awarded three Dana-Farber scientists grants totaling $525,000 to promote research on the blood cancer multiple myeloma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation sustains momentum in multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Multiple myeloma treatments have significantly improved over the past two decades, thanks in part to the driving engine of transformational philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Oetgen Family invests in early detection and intervention for myeloma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has launched a revolution in myeloma care, thanks to the power of precision medicine, genomics, immunotherapy, and philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Cyrena Musset

In September 2025, dreams became reality as more than 200 participants, including Dana-Farber patients, had the once-in-a lifetime chance to play ball at Fenway Park. Thanks to generous support from sponsors, the Boston Red Sox, fundraising teams, and donors, Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised more than $200,000 to strike out cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised $230,000 to support innovative cancer research and compassionate patient care at Dana-Farber. Thanks to donor support, Dana-Farber patients and their families were able to participate in this unforgettable experience and take the field at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Milestone 20th annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon raises $3.5 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1953, the Boston Red Sox have had a deep and multifaceted impact on patients with cancer through its strong partnership with Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber patient and doctor on the field at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Strike Out Cancer with the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As the Red Sox returned to Fenway Park this spring, the Jimmy Fund community came together to cheer them on and support Dana-Farber patients. Rally Against CancerSM teams celebrated Opening Day on March 30 and more than 100 fans signed up to strike out cancer by donating for every Red…

img.alt_text: Boston Red Sox and The Jimmy Fund

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation honored with the Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Expect Miracles Foundation (EMF) received the 2025 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—during a special on-field ceremony at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Group photo of Jimmy Fund Award winners and Dana-Farber staff at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge celebrates PMC Pedal Partners from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Fenway Park
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 17, dozens of PMC Pedal Partners—pediatric patients from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute paired with PMC riders and teams—gathered at The 521 Overlook at Fenway Park to meet the cyclists participating in the 46th PMC on Aug. 2 and 3.

img.alt_text: A family of four at Fenway Park

Spring 2026
By Caitlin Roberts

Jimmy Fund Little League presented by the Yawkey Foundation surpassed its $275,000 goal, contributing $359,476 of unrestricted funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and underscoring the Yawkey Foundation’s dedication to advancing care for its community. The top fundraising team was North Reading 10U Gold, raising $18,465, and the top individual fundraiser, James Keohan, raised $10,617.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Yawkey Foundation’s heartfelt support
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Yawkey Foundation is a longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, stemming from the historic relationship between the Jimmy Fund and the Boston Red Sox. Perpetuating the philanthropic legacy of the team’s owners, Tom and Jean Yawkey, the foundation made gifts totaling $180,000 in 2024.

img.alt_text: Two people holding ice cream outside a Cookie Monstah food truck

jetpack-related-posts.title: Yawkey Foundation supports patients and staff
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 1953, Tom and Jean Yawkey initiated what would become a legacy of remarkable support by helping to establish the historic relationship between the Boston Red Sox, Sidney Farber, MD, and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: People pose for a photo in front of a food truck

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Golf community helps to usher in the Jimmy Fund’s 75th
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun marked another ace year in 2023, with an array of dedicated tournament directors, sponsors, and supporters across the country raising more than $6.8 million for The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports raised more than $272,000 for Dana-Farber in its 39th season. New England’s young baseball and softball players extended their Little League® seasons to take a swing at cancer by raising vital funds for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Establishing an endowment is a powerful way to support The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports raised $281,332 in 2023 for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber. Every year, Little League baseball and softball players in New England raise vital funds for the Jimmy Fund during this summer league, making a significant impact in the fight against cancer.

Spring 2026
By Tarice Gray

The Esther A. & Joseph Klingenstein Fund gave $450,000 through the Klingenstein Fellowship Awards in Neuroscience to support the research of Xin Gu, PhD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This vital funding enables Gu to investigate the midnolin-proteasome pathway, to advance understanding of brain function and cancer treatment, and drive progress toward improved patient outcomes worldwide.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Hannah White Hannah

A $150,000 grant from the Lung Cancer Research Foundation supports William Feng, PhD, in investigating AP-1 transcription factors as a potential “Achilles’ heel” in KRAS-mutant lung cancer. His research aims to develop a novel AP-1–targeted therapy to overcome drug resistance and improve outcomes for patients with this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating treatment-resistant lung cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A collaborative, multi-institution team led by Dana-Farber’s David Barbie, MD, received a four-year, $2.5 million grant from the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) and Lung Cancer Research Foundation (LCRF) for researching a cure for non-small cell lung carcinoma.

img.alt_text: IASLC Lung Cancer Research Foundation logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Clifford Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Clifford Family established the Woolley-Clifford Foundation Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the research of David Kozono, MD, PhD, as he works to investigate blood and tissue-based biomarkers in lung cancer patients that can help predict lung inflammation and anti-tumor response following radiation therapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New grants advance key research across multiple disease areas
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime Dana-Farber supporter Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, recently awarded $1.45 million to support seven researchers pursuing projects in a wide range of disease areas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gail and Ralph Reynolds
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gail and Ralph Reynolds made a gift of $100,000 to support the work of Julia Rotow, MD, and Matt Oser, MD, PhD, who are collaborating to pioneer novel treatments for lung neuroendocrine cancer. By harnessing proteins previously considered “undruggable,” they aim to improve options for patients with this complex cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White

With this gift, Sands, along with researcher Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, will work to identify biomarkers to personalize treatment and track response to therapy in patients with small…

title.rendered: Matthew Larson Foundation for Pediatric Brain Tumors

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Bethany Herrama

The Matthew Larson Foundation for Pediatric Brain Tumors awarded $450,000 to Pratiti (Mimi) Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, to advance research aimed at overcoming therapeutic resistance in pediatric brain tumors. Such pivotal support empowers her team to accelerate discoveries with the potential to deliver more effective treatments for  young patients, honoring Matt’s legacy and inspiring hope.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF accelerates research to better treat pediatric brain tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1991, Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation (PBTF) has helped patients and families cope with a brain cancer diagnosis, offering financial, logistical, and emotional support.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Team Jack Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Team Jack Foundation has donated $400,000 to Pratiti (Mimi) Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, for her research on pediatric low-grade gliomas (pLGGs). Her project aims to uncover interactions between tumor drivers and brain development, potentially leading to innovative treatments. This collaboration promises new insights into pLGG growth and therapeutic strategies for affected…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Janower family drives pediatric brain tumor research forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cindy and AJ Janower’s introduction to the challenging world of childhood cancer began when their daughter, Samantha “Sammi,” was just three years old.

img.alt_text: A family of five posing outside

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation has awarded grants totaling $395,000 to fund pediatric cancer research by Institute researchers Rahela Aziz-Bose, MD, and Jun Qi, PhD. The grants will support their research to better understand and tackle barriers to nutrition for childhood cancer survivors and identify novel targets for pediatric brain tumors and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Curing Kids Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Curing Kids Cancer has donated $300,000 to Jun Qi, PhD, for his research on group 3 medulloblastomas (G3 MB). His team aims to develop a brain-penetrating EP300/CBP bromodomain inhibitor, offering a promising therapeutic option for these aggressive pediatric brain tumors, potentially transforming treatment from bench to bedside.

Spring 2026
By Casey Repasy

Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance the studies of uveal melanoma and immunotherapy-resistant melanoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor made a generous $100,000 commitment, renewing their support of melanoma research under the leadership of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Their impactful philanthropy is driving innovative studies in immunotherapy, including those targeting anti-tumor immunity, aiming to uncover new treatments and improve outcomes for melanoma patients worldwide.

img.alt_text: Three people in a Dana-Farber exam room

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kittredges continue generous support of melanoma and immuno-oncology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Francis Kittredge, MD, JD, and his wife, Adele, know that supporting Dana-Farber Cancer Institute makes a difference because their philanthropy already has—and their impact continues to grow through their ongoing generosity.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Melanoma Research Foundation has awarded Dana-Farber’s Pere Puigserver, PhD, with a prestigious $200,000 Established Investigator Award. Puigserver’s pioneering research aims to revolutionize immunotherapeutic approaches for metastatic melanoma, with a focus on overcoming drug resistance and improving patient survival outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rare eye cancer is focus of new fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jonathan and Shelley Isaacson have made a $1 million gift to establish Dana-Farber’s first fellowship dedicated to the study of the disease, The Isaacson Family Fellowship in Ocular Melanoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Micki and Steven Hirsch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Clinical trials are considered essential for groundbreaking research. To help advance Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s clinical trials, Micki and Steven Hirsch made a gift of $100,000 to the Hirsch Family Fund for the Office of Clinical Research. Jeffrey Meyerhardt, MD, MPH, FASCO, leads the program which has benefited from the generous…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael Swidler
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received a gracious contribution from Michael Swidler to establish the Nancy Swidler Fund for Breast Cancer Research in honor of his late wife. Managed by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, this fund is intended to advance pioneering breast cancer research and create pathways to better outcomes for every…

jetpack-related-posts.title: David Liposarcoma Research Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In September, the inaugural David Liposarcoma Research Initiative International Scientific Symposium was held at Dana-Farber. The symposium included the unveiling of a plaque commemorating the generous pledge from the Rossy Foundation that, through The Rossy Foundation Fund at KBF Canada, established the David Liposarcoma Research Initiative under the direction of…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquering blood cancers is focus of Blood Cancer United grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, nearly 200,000 Americans are diagnosed with leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, or another bloodborne cancer. Blood Cancer United has awarded $4.2 million in grants to eight Dana-Farber physician-scientists working to better understand, treat, and potentially cure these often deadly diseases.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Kerr’s generous gift of $100,000 to the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research supports the groundbreaking work of James Cleary, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Their contribution will help advance innovative treatment approaches for gastrointestinal cancers, underscoring their vital role in transforming patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ellice and David Vittor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their gift of $150,000, Ellice and David Vittor established the Vittor Family Research Fund to advance research by Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. The Bing Center is the largest center in the world dedicated to researching this rare blood cancer.

Spring 2026
By Lucy McDonald

The Sally Naser Charitable Foundation, led by Camille and Robert Naser, made a $200,000 gift in support of early career investigators whose research drives breakthroughs, improves patient outcomes, and advances pediatric sarcoma care and research. This gift builds upon many years of support in honor of their daughter, Sally.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Crystal Family Charitable Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Crystal Family Charitable Foundation recently made a generous $200,000 gift to support a variety of research and patient care programs at Dana-Farber. The funds will drive innovative prostate and pancreatic cancer research while enhancing social services offered to pediatric patients and grieving families.

img.alt_text: Three people pose for a photo in front of mountains

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation gift focuses on cancer interception
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $1.25 million gift to Dana-Farber from the Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation supports research focused on ways pancreatic cancer might be detected—and intercepted—before it can be seen on CT scans or other imaging modalities.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift continues donor’s legacy by supporting gastrointestinal research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Throughout her life, Ilene Beal was dedicated to hard work and breaking down barriers. She became a female pioneer in the Boston banking world and was a valued mentor for other women in the industry.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon supports bold research by emerging talent
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded $1.22 million in grants to four early career investigators at Dana-Farber whose research has the potential to yield important breakthroughs in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers.

Spring 2026
By Lucy McDonald

The Optica Foundation Challenge Prize awarded $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Fay Nicholson, PhD, providing her with critical funding to advance her groundbreaking research in enhancing surgical precision. This support accelerates discoveries and exemplifies both Dana-Farber and the foundation’s commitment to empowering transformative cancer research that improves patient outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate gift accelerates cancer care and research for years to come
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Out of gratitude for the excellent care received by his late wife, Gerry Martineau left a generous bequest to support research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation spurs pivotal research aimed at new epigenetic therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is spurring Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s efforts to eradicate difficult-to-treat cancers through recent grants totaling $1.6 million awarded to two Dana-Farber investigators who aim to develop novel treatments known as epigenetic therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: International Myeloma Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Mohammad Rashidian, PhD, received a $250,000 Translational Research Award from the International Myeloma Society and the Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation. This support will advance his innovative work to combat disease relapse in multiple myeloma patients following CAR T-cell therapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Micki and Steven Hirsch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Clinical trials are considered essential for groundbreaking research. To help advance Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s clinical trials, Micki and Steven Hirsch made a gift of $100,000 to the Hirsch Family Fund for the Office of Clinical Research. Jeffrey Meyerhardt, MD, MPH, FASCO, leads the program which has benefited from the generous…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers.

Spring 2026
By Brendan Monahan

Ravestock Boston, hosted in October by the William Raveis Charitable Fund, raised nearly $150,000 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s life-changing mission. Held in memory of Meghan Raveis, the event brought together community and live music to benefit Dana-Farber’s cancer research and care, while honoring Meghan’s legacy of service to others.

Spring 2026
By Tarice Gray

The estate of Robert Rosenthal, PhD, known as a father of meta-analysis and one of the 20th century’s top 100 psychologists, left a $174,000 gift to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. He had a special devotion to research and patient care, which are the areas this gift will support.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A home run for hope: A Father’s tribute advances pediatric research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The late Robert P. Cingolani, DPM—affectionately known as “Doc”—was a dedicated physician, devoted father, and cherished community member. He made a transformative $2 million estate gift to support pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in memory of his son, Michael, who passed away from bone cancer at the age…

img.alt_text: Researchers at work in the Centers for Early Detection and Interception.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Belfers aim to make immunotherapy effective for more patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: An extraordinary gift of $10 million from Robert and Renée Belfer and family will support innovative immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Endowed fellowship looks to the future
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Baila Janock embodies generosity in its many forms. For over 30 years, she has combined her gifts of time, treasure, and talent to make a long-lasting impact on Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and its patients.

content.rendered:
Spring 2026
By Tarice Gray

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received a gracious contribution from Michael Swidler to establish the Nancy Swidler Fund for Breast Cancer Research in honor of his late wife. Managed by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, this fund is intended to advance pioneering breast cancer research and create pathways to better outcomes for every patient.

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Barbara Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jonathan Mehlman
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jonathan Mehlman gave $100,000, honoring his late wife Marla, in support of breast cancer research under the direction of Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH. With this funding, Tolaney and her team will continue developing new clinical approaches for the most aggressive forms of breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor, a non-profit organization that funds important research for stage IV metastatic breast cancer (MBC), has awarded research grants totaling $700,000 to three Dana-Farber faculty members

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

By Caitlin Roberts

Raising over $3.8 million since 1996, the organization continues to “Make Waves to Fight Cancer” and fuel critical survivorship research at Dana-Farber. This year’s event will be Aug. 15, 2026.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America raised $250,000 in 2024 to benefit Dana-Farber’s Perini Family Survivors’ Center. Since 1996, the Boston Open Water Swim has united swimmers of all ages and abilities, raising over $3.5 million in total to support vital survivorship research at Dana-Farber and continuing to “Make Waves Against Cancer.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America hosted their 28th annual Boston Open Water Swim event, which directly benefits Dana-Farber patients and families. Swimmers of all ages and skills levels united to “Make Waves Against Cancer” and raised $175,000, bringing the event’s cumulative fundraising total to over $3 million to date.
