content.rendered:
Winter 2025 
Photography by John Deputy 

Before December 31: 

MAKE A GIFT THAT’S MATCHED 

Take advantage of our year-end matching challenge to support cancer research and care. When you donate to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund today, your gift doubles, thanks to a matching challenge from Arbella Insurance Group. And if your New Year’s resolution is to start a monthly gift, all your 2026 recurring gifts will be matched, up to $10,000! 

STOCK AND SECURITIES 

If you make a gift of appreciated securities before the end of the calendar year, you may be entitled to a charitable deduction on this year’s federal income taxes and may also avoid capital gains tax on the appreciation of the asset. These tax savings could increase the value of your gift to Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund at a decreased cost to you. Through a partnership with The Boston Foundation, you can also donate privately held C-Corp stock for the benefit of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. 

INDIVIDUAL RETIREMENT ACCOUNT (IRA) 

If you are 70½ or older, you can give up to $108,000 to Dana-Farber directly from your IRA without paying income taxes on the transfer. Plus, if you are 73 or older, your gift may satisfy your required minimum distribution and lower your taxable income. No matter your age, you can designate Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund as the beneficiary of all or a percentage of your IRA and it will pass to us tax-free after your lifetime. 

DONOR-ADVISED FUND (DAF) 

Now is a great time to distribute a donation to Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund from your DAF. Recommend a grant from your DAF by December 31 to fuel groundbreaking discoveries and initiatives into the new year. You can name Dana-Farber as a beneficiary of your donor-advised fund as well! 

REVIEW AND UPDATE ACCOUNT BENEFICIARIES 

The end of the year is a great time to review beneficiary designations on your bank, investment, and retirement accounts. Of course, loved ones are the first people to consider. After that, providing for causes you care about like Dana-Farber is an excellent way to demonstrate your values and make an impact on future generations. 

To learn more, visit jimmyfund.org/get-involved/give.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Here are five charitable things to consider before the end of the calendar year, to advance Dana-Farber's cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Society (DFS) is a group of visionary donors who are changing lives and creating a legacy through a planned gift such as a bequest, life income gift, or beneficiary designation to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, the Jimmy Fund, the Friends of Dana-Farber, or the Pan-Mass Challenge.

jetpack-related-posts.title: 2025 PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the nation’s single most successful athletic fundraiser and Dana-Farber’s largest single contributor, kicked off its 2025 fundraising year at the 10th PMC Winter Cycle on Feb. 1 at Fenway Park.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge makes record-breaking $78 million gift to drive Dana-Farber’s progress against cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), a bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the world, has built an unparalleled track record for success strengthened by touchstone traditions and continuous improvements in pursuit of the goal of defying cancer.

content.rendered:
Winter 2025
By Ross Perry

ALK Positive has gifted a generous grant to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Alice Shaw, MD, PhD’s, pioneering research on methylthioadenosine phosphorylase loss in ALK-positive lung cancer. This vital funding will drive innovative strategies to improve patient outcomes, empowering breakthroughs that enhance care for individuals affected by ALK-positive lung cancer worldwide.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V is for victory over intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Georgette and John Heerwagen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Georgette and John Heerwagen recently renewed their support for lung cancer research at Dana-Farber with a generous gift of $125,000. Under the direction of David Jackman, MD, in collaboration with David Barbie, MD, both faculty in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber, this funding will enable researchers to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Prevention Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Prevention Initiative (CPI) awarded $450,000 to Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, for her breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, targeting early tumor progression. This grant highlights CPI’s vital support for and shared mission with Dana-Farber in advancing impactful strategies for early medical interception of inherited cancer to improve…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Optica Foundation Challenge
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Optica Foundation Challenge Prize awarded $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Fay Nicholson, PhD, providing her with critical funding to advance her groundbreaking research in enhancing surgical precision. This support accelerates discoveries and exemplifies both Dana-Farber and the foundation’s commitment to empowering transformative cancer research that improves patient outcomes.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, honored with endowed chair
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A generous group of Trustees, colleagues, friends, and supporters contributed over $3 million to establish the chair and commemorate Glimcher’s legacy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American-Italian Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American-Italian Cancer Foundation, a New York-based nonprofit that funds postdoctorate research fellowships for Italian scientists, provided $120,000 in support of Dana-Farber researchers Edoardo Garbo, MD, and Francesco Paoloni, MD. Their lung cancer research aligns with the foundation’s mission to advance treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes.

title.rendered: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation

content.rendered:
Winter 2025
By Kayla McMahon

The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation awarded $125,000 to Genevra Kuziel, PhD, supporting her research on estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer, the most common breast cancer subtype with a high recurrence rate. Kuziel’s work aims to develop innovative combination therapies, with the goal of transforming treatment options and improving outcomes for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation recently made grants totaling $200,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to fund two studies. One explores circulating tumor DNA at critical timepoints in early stage hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and the second assesses how chemotherapy effects the tumor-immune microenvironment and estrogen receptor activity in young…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation gave $125,000 in support of research led by Paolo Tarantino, MD, which seeks to improve the precision of antibody-drug conjugates. This funding will aid Tarantino in unlocking new insights into metastatic breast cancer, with the intention of identifying additional treatments for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Breast Cancer Alliance awarded a 2024 Young Investigator Grant of $125,000 to Sarah Naomi Olsen, PhD, accelerating her research on chromatin complexes in estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. This impactful award will deepen our understanding of these unique complexes, laying the groundwork for new treatments which could significantly improve patient…

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor, a non-profit organization that funds important research for stage IV metastatic breast cancer (MBC), has awarded research grants totaling $700,000 to three Dana-Farber faculty members

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

content.rendered:
Winter 2025
By Casey Repasy
Photography by Josh Campbell

Craig and Bettina Burr gave $100,000 towards the Bettina and Craig Burr Breast Cancer Genetics and Prevention Research Fund at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This gift will support the research of Judy Garber, MD, MPH, the Susan F. Smith Chair at Dana-Farber, and Myles Brown, MD, the Emil Frei III, MD, Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School, which focuses on BRCA2-associated cancers to improve prevention and treatment through hormone blockers and tumor type prediction.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation grants more than $4 million to speed Dana-Farber research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Building on past support, BCRF recently made grants totaling more than $4 million to 12 physician-scientists at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: BRCA gene mutations are focus of $1 million research fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Donna and John Hale donated $1 million earlier this year to establish a research fund in support of The Mellen and Eisenson Family Center for BRCA and Related Genes. It will be managed by Judy Garber, MD, MPH, Susan F. Smith Chair and chief of the Division of Cancer Genetics…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Gray Foundation empowers team science against BRCA-mutated cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Philanthropy has transformative power to address society’s intractable challenges. The Gray Foundation is committed to this goal and, with two grants totaling nearly $6 million, is harnessing this power for good through The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Barbara Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chubb gift advances ctDNA research for cancer detection and therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $750,000 gift, Patricia and Steve Chubb established The Alice Fund to support Parsons’ research into ctDNA and her lab’s efforts to develop technologies to overcome current limitations.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Campaign leadership spurs innovation and progress at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Motivated by a desire to ease the burden of cancer for future patients, the leaders of The Dana-Farber Campaign have dedicated their time and leveraged their expertise and connections for the entirety of this ambitious, multi-year fundraising effort.

content.rendered:
Winter 2025
By Kayla McMahon

The Cancer Prevention Initiative (CPI) awarded $450,000 to Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, for her breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, targeting early tumor progression. This grant highlights CPI’s vital support for and shared mission with Dana-Farber in advancing impactful strategies for early medical interception of inherited cancer to improve patient outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society targets improved treatments and access
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded $1.12 million in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers seeking to answer those questions and more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor, a non-profit organization that funds important research for stage IV metastatic breast cancer (MBC), has awarded research grants totaling $700,000 to three Dana-Farber faculty members

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding by the late Evelyn Lauder alongside her dear friend Larry Norton, MD, in 1993, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF) has championed research as the key to one day curing breast cancer.

Winter 2025
By Bethany Herrema

The Children’s Cancer Research Fund made two grants totaling $350,000 to support an early phase trial for relapsed pediatric liver cancer led by Allison O’Neill, MD, and liquid biopsy research in rhabdomyosarcoma led by Brian Crompton, MD. These pivotal resources help to develop more effective precision therapies for children facing aggressive cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation has awarded a $200,000 research grant to Brian Crompton, MD, for his work to test a prognostic liquid biopsy approach for pediatric Ewing sarcoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PHASE ONE Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PHASE ONE Foundation awarded $370,000 to support a Dana-Farber clinical trial led by Alison O’Neill, MD. The clinical trial aims to test a new intratumoral delivery method for a novel immunotherapy in pediatric patients with relapsed or refractory solid tumors.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palumbo family moves needle for patients with rare pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On the cusp of Chad Palumbo’s senior year of high school in 2022, he found himself in an unexpected place: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Chad had been diagnosed with rhabdomyosarcoma, a rare form of soft tissue cancer that appears mainly in children and teens.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lee and Alexandria Zachos
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Lee and Alexandria Zachos made a gift of $100,000 to The Vasilios Kafkes Fund for Pediatric Cancer Research II at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, supporting Brian Crompton, MD, to advance ctDNA testing in pediatric tumors–a noninvasive blood test to improve detection, prevention, and care in childhood cancers–by developing a clinical assay…

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation has awarded grants totaling $395,000 to fund pediatric cancer research by Institute researchers Rahela Aziz-Bose, MD, and Jun Qi, PhD. The grants will support their research to better understand and tackle barriers to nutrition for childhood cancer survivors and identify novel targets for pediatric brain tumors and…

Winter 2025
By Cyrena Musset

The Cure Alzheimer’s Fund awarded $201,250 to Peter Sicinski, MD, PhD, to advance his research on anticancer compounds that may reverse Alzheimer’s symptoms. His work focuses on preclinical validation, investigating their potential to restore memory and synaptic health, and uncovering molecular mechanisms—offering hope for transformative Alzheimer’s treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Advancing Parkinson’s research: Spiegelman’s groundbreaking work
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: From a remarkable act of generosity, the Tyler Family has donated $3 million to establish the Tyler Family Fund for Parkinson's Research, supporting the groundbreaking work of Bruce Spiegelman, PhD, the Stanley J. Korsmeyer, MD, Professor of Cell Biology and Medicine at Harvard Medical School.

jetpack-related-posts.title: 3000 Miles to a Cure
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: 3000 Miles to a Cure awarded $100,000 to support the ALLELE-GBM research program at Dana-Farber, under the direction of Keith Ligon, MD, PhD. Ligon’s team is working to put genomic data into the hands of patients, providers, and researchers to advance treatments and clinical trials in glioblastoma (GBM).

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Cancer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: National Cancer Center awarded fellowship grants to Dana-Farber totaling $328,000. One new grant will support Katharina Hoebel, MD, PhD, in developing personalized treatment for non-small cell lung cancer through the use of artificial intelligence. With a second new commitment, Diego Martinez Alonso, PhD, will explore how to utilize CDK4/6 inhibitors…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquering blood cancers is focus of Blood Cancer United grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, nearly 200,000 Americans are diagnosed with leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, or another bloodborne cancer. Blood Cancer United has awarded $4.2 million in grants to eight Dana-Farber physician-scientists working to better understand, treat, and potentially cure these often deadly diseases.

Winter 2025
By Ross Perry

Hallie and John Dovich generously gifted $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, establishing the John and Hallie Dovich Fund. Under the direction of Vincent Ho, MD, this fund will support stem cell transplantation research, to improve transplant outcomes for patients with for patients with myelofibrosis and other blood cancers, ultimately enhancing patient care and treatment strategies.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2022, Andrea McGrath celebrated 20 years since her successful stem cell transplant at Dana-Farber. She hosted a survivorship event, raising over $16,000 to benefit the work of her doctor and now friend, Corey Cutler, MD, MPH, FRCPC, whose advances in stem cell transplantation are continuing to improve outcomes for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Bill Pomeroy gives the gift of access to patients with blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After his successful transplant, Pomeroy was inspired to help create better outcomes for patients like him. In 2005, he founded the William G. Pomeroy Foundation® to raise awareness and fund initiatives to improve access to blood cancer care. Pomeroy and his foundation have since made gifts totaling more than $1…

img.alt_text: Bill Pomeroy with William G. Pomeroy Foundation banners

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Marrow Donor Program
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The NMDP provided a $400,000 grant to support the research of Nicoletta Cieri, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This funding will support her work to improve allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation by identifying genetic factors influencing graft-versus-host disease, potentially leading to more personalized treatment strategies and improved patient outcomes.

Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

With her $100,000 gift, she hopes Cleary can help patients like her defy this rare…

Winter 2025
By Bethany Herrema

The Charles H. Hood Foundation awarded Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc, a generous $200,000 grant to study a combination treatment for acute myeloid leukemia targeting oncogenic fusion proteins and foster her career development as an independent investigator. This funding supports high-risk, high-reward pediatric studies, enabling groundbreaking discoveries, improved care, and ideally better outcomes for young patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cure Childhood Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc, received a $220,000 Early Investigator Award from CURE Childhood Cancer. This generous grant supports her research focused on determining whether targeting two proteins can effectively treat a specific type of acute myeloid leukemia. The grant also helps launch her career as an…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society attacks rare and resistant blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS) has awarded six grants totaling $5.8 million to Dana-Farber investigators.

img.alt_text: An artist’s rendering of bone marrow cells showing acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research awarded $250,000 to Dana-Farber’s Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, who is exploring the biology of cohesin mutations, frequent and recurrent drivers of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia. With this funding, Tothova aims to develop targeted treatments for these cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquering blood cancers is focus of Blood Cancer United grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, nearly 200,000 Americans are diagnosed with leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, or another bloodborne cancer. Blood Cancer United has awarded $4.2 million in grants to eight Dana-Farber physician-scientists working to better understand, treat, and potentially cure these often deadly diseases.

Winter 2025
By Bethany Herrema

The Exon 20 Group’s International Research Consortium at the International Cancer Advocacy Network (ICAN) awarded $100,000 to Michael Eck, MD, PhD, to improve our understanding of common EGFR exon 20 insertion variants, which will be valuable for the development of potent and selective inhibitors for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. This funding can accelerate the development of new therapies and the delivery of improved treatments to increase patient quality of life.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lyn Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Lyn Green gave $100,000 to support EGFR lung cancer research led by Julia Rotow, MD. Her generous contribution bolsters work around this genetic mutation, including efforts to refine a blood test for relapse monitoring and for improving treatments. This research has the potential to significantly improve patient care and outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jeffrey and Jennifer Goldstein
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jeffrey and Jennifer Goldstein made a generous gift in support of Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, director of the Carole M. and Philip L. Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber. The gift will support Jänne and his team’s continued research into targeted therapies in lung cancer, novel EGFR inhibitors, and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society targets improved treatments and access
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded $1.12 million in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers seeking to answer those questions and more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Prevention Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Prevention Initiative (CPI) awarded $450,000 to Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, for her breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, targeting early tumor progression. This grant highlights CPI’s vital support for and shared mission with Dana-Farber in advancing impactful strategies for early medical interception of inherited cancer to improve…

content.rendered:
Winter 2025
By Brendan Monahan

The Lymphoma Research Foundation awarded Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Tianfang Ma, PhD, a generous $195,000 Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant, to bolster his research and growth as an independent investigator. Ma’s work focuses on the tumor immune microenvironment in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and may help enhance immunotherapy effectiveness and identify predictive markers to improve patient outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquering blood cancers is focus of Blood Cancer United grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, nearly 200,000 Americans are diagnosed with leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, or another bloodborne cancer. Blood Cancer United has awarded $4.2 million in grants to eight Dana-Farber physician-scientists working to better understand, treat, and potentially cure these often deadly diseases.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Mark Foundation spurs innovation in immunotherapy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research has awarded Dana-Farber investigator Catherine Wu, MD, and two investigators at the Broad Institute a $3 million, three-year grant to further their research into personalized, T cell-directed cancer immunotherapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Research Institute invests in the people behind basic research discoveries in cancer immunology
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: While the immune system is inherently able to identify and destroy harmful cells, tumors often develop ways to interrupt anti-cancer immune activity. Restoring this powerful effect in order to defeat cancer through therapies that galvanize the immune system has transformed the treatment trajectory and potential for cure in many cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CRI grants accelerate immunotherapy research at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Research Institute (CRI) is advancing bold new strategies to harness the immune system against cancer through two grants at DanaFarber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Human Frontier Science Program
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Human Frontier Science Program, an organization that promotes international collaboration in basic research, awarded grants totaling more than $400,000 to fund biochemistry research at Dana-Farber. Winter 2025
By Brendan Monahan

The Neuroendocrine Tumor Research Foundation granted a generous $270,000 Investigator Award to Ramesh Shivdasani, MD, PhD, Dana-Farber’s Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, Chair. This funding supports innovative studies to model intestinal neuroendocrine tumor biology, identify therapeutic targets, and bring more treatment options and hope to patients with these complex cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, honored with endowed chair
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A generous group of Trustees, colleagues, friends, and supporters contributed over $3 million to establish the chair and commemorate Glimcher’s legacy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

img.alt_text: T cells (white) lining for an attack on human triple-negative breast cancer cells (red and yellow)

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Impact You Have Made Possible
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute aspires to provide the care and treatment our patients deserve. We are able to achieve these ambitions because of our dedicated donor community.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Foley Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Foley Family made a gift of $100,000 to advance research into paragangliomas, a rare type of neuroendocrine tumor, led by Kimberly Perez, MD. Their gift will support experimental studies including the first clinical trial analyzing better treatments for patients with hereditary and non-hereditary paragangliomas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF accelerates research to better treat pediatric brain tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1991, Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation (PBTF) has helped patients and families cope with a brain cancer diagnosis, offering financial, logistical, and emotional support.

Winter 2025
By Lucy McDonald
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

The Pew Charitable Trusts provided $430,000 in support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers Evanna Mills, PhD, and Brenda Nakagaki, PhD. jetpack-related-posts.title: Anna Fuller Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Anna Fuller Fund has made a wonderful impact with a $150,000 gift to support breast cancer research conducted by Evanna Mills, PhD, at Dana-Farber. The investment will fuel investigations to better understand risk factors for triple-negative breast cancer with the potential to inform the development of more effective treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grant fuels research into the new field of immunometabolism
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Dana-Farber seeks to better understand and manipulate immunometabolism, which is emerging as an important frontier with potential to advance treatments for metabolic and inflammatory diseases including cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mathers Foundation grants promote basic cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Many of today’s important advances in cancer care trace their origins to basic research—a form of scientific investigation aimed at uncovering the fundamental principles of biology, chemistry, and foundational science.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Basic research is focus of Mathers Charitable Foundation grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The G. Harold and Leila Y. Mathers Charitable Foundation has awarded Dana-Farber $1.47 million to support two Institute researchers investigating how cancer develops and how cells detect and respond to viral infections.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society targets improved treatments and access
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded $1.12 million in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers seeking to answer those questions and more.

content.rendered:
Winter 2025
By Bethany Herrema

St. Baldrick’s Foundation awarded a $195,000 fellowship grant to Geoffrey Smith, MD, PhD, to try to identify mechanisms of immune evasion in models of osteosarcoma using next generation sequencing and cutting-edge technologies to study the response of single cells. Based on these findings, he will test novel immunotherapies to prioritize the next generation of osteosarcoma human clinical trials.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lymphoma Research Foundation awarded Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's Tianfang Ma, PhD, a generous $195,000 Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant, to bolster his research and growth as an independent investigator. Ma’s work focuses on the tumor immune microenvironment in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and may help enhance immunotherapy effectiveness and identify predictive markers…

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation awarded a total of $415,000 to Dana-Farber studies into how neuroblastoma, one of the most common pediatric solid tumors, escapes destruction by the immune system; and how a category of newly discovered “dark proteins” may point toward new approaches to treat medulloblastoma, a devastating form of childhood…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation grants millions to advance childhood cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It all began over 20 years ago with a simple, yet profound, act of kindness by Alex Scott, a determined little girl with cancer, who held a lemonade stand fundraiser to help other kids like her and inspired countless others to do the same.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Pancreatic Cancer Action Network
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pancreatic Cancer Action Network recently awarded $400,000 in grant funding to Institute researchers Julien Dilly, MS, and William Freed-Pastor, MD, PhD, to better understand mechanisms of response and resistance to KRAS inhibition in pancreatic cancer and improve existing pre-clinical models for this intractable disease.

Winter 2025
By Elyse Pleickhardt

A $250,000 gift from Rachel Teller and her late husband, Jonathan Teller—made together before Jonathan’s untimely passing this summer—will help drive pioneering research led by Cigall Kadoch, PhD, into synovial sarcoma and other rare diseases that urgently need better treatments and cures. This deeply personal commitment reflects the Tellers’ shared wish to make a lasting difference for patients and families facing these rare, formidable diagnoses.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift from Haroun Family drives critical research for adult patients with Ewing sarcoma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rob Haroun and his wife, Julie, established the Haroun Family Fund with a generous gift of $1 million. Under the leadership of Suzanne George, MD, chief of the Division of Sarcoma, the fund will support innovative research aimed at discovering the next breakthroughs in treating Ewing sarcoma in adults.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rare eye cancer is focus of new fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jonathan and Shelley Isaacson have made a $1 million gift to establish Dana-Farber’s first fellowship dedicated to the study of the disease, The Isaacson Family Fellowship in Ocular Melanoma.

img.alt_text: Three people in a Dana-Farber lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber faculty are part of “grand challenge” to defeat childhood tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has been awarded more than $3 million in funding as part of a Cancer Grand Challenge to find new treatments for solid tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jeannie and Jonathan Lavine Endowed Chairs for Preventive Cancer Therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2020, Jeannie and Jonathan Lavine endowed three Dana-Farber Chairs in support of prevention and early detection research at the Institute, with a gift to The Dana-Farber Campaign.

img.alt_text: Catherine Wu, MD; Laurie H. Glimcher, MD; and Jonathan Lavine

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick made a generous gift to support pancreatic cancer research by Srivatsan Raghavan, MD, PhD, before Kevin’s passing from pancreatic cancer in July 2023. This generous contribution reflects their desire to help Dana-Farber uncover new treatment options and improve outcomes for all patients facing pancreatic cancer.

img.alt_text: Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick sitting on a rock in front of the ocean

Anne Marie and Salvatore Torregrossa made a generous $100,000 gift to support pediatric cancer research and care led by Lisa Diller, MD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Winter 2025
By Hannah White Hannah
Photography by Sam Ogden

Stephani Batchelor and Andrew Robert Whittaker made an additional gift of $225,000 to Dana-Farber’s Lynch Syndrome Center. This gift supports the leadership of Sapna Syngal, MD, MPH, and Matthew Yurgelun, MD, FASCO, CGAF, and their team in diagnosing Lynch syndrome and advancing screenings, treatments, and prevention strategies to help patients live long, healthy lives.

Winter 2025
By Casey Repasy

Lee and Alexandria Zachos made a gift of $100,000 to The Vasilios Kafkes Fund for Pediatric Cancer Research II at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, supporting Brian Crompton, MD, to advance ctDNA testing in pediatric tumors–a noninvasive blood test to improve detection, prevention, and care in childhood cancers–by developing a clinical assay to be used as a standard of care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Little Warrior Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Little Warrior Foundation has granted $100,000 to Brian Crompton, MD, to develop a CLIA/CAP-certified pediatric-specific circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) assay. This non-invasive test aims to detect pediatric-specific cancer mutations that will be helpful in monitoring treatment response and may one day allow for risk stratification at diagnosis—helping clinicians tailor treatment…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Anne Marie & Salvatore Torregrossa
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Anne Marie and Salvatore Torregrossa made a generous $100,000 gift to support pediatric cancer research and care led by Lisa Diller, MD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Their contribution will help advance groundbreaking discoveries and improve care for children facing cancer, continuing Torregrossa’s legacy of compassion and commitment to our lifesaving…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises over $760,000 for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This spring, New England Stop & Shop customers donated over $760,000 to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber through the grocery chain’s annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation has awarded a $200,000 research grant to Brian Crompton, MD, for his work to test a prognostic liquid biopsy approach for pediatric Ewing sarcoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber faculty are part of “grand challenge” to defeat childhood tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has been awarded more than $3 million in funding as part of a Cancer Grand Challenge to find new treatments for solid tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: New England Stop & Shop customers donated $1.4 million to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber last year during the grocery chain’s 31st annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign, which has raised a total of $77 million for the Institute since 1991.

content.rendered:
Winter 2025

Dear Friends,

As I reflect on this past year, I am filled with immense gratitude for the generosity and unwavering commitment of our Dana-Farber community. Your steadfast support has been a driving force behind so many of our achievements, and it is because of you that we have been able to navigate challenges and embrace new opportunities with hope and determination.

This year brought unexpected uncertainties due to changes in federal policy. However, your belief in our mission never wavered. Your dedication has enabled us to continue our vital work and celebrate remarkable milestones, including the installment of eight leaders into endowed chair and professorship positions. These endowed positions, made possible by your philanthropy, provide permanent funding that will sustain groundbreaking scientific and clinical advancements for generations to come. Together, we are opening doors to extraordinary possibilities, and we are premiering a new section in this issue that highlights some of this work.

We are especially grateful for unrestricted gifts that empower us to innovate and expand our efforts in research and treatment. The largest donor for unrestricted gifts is the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), which we are proud to feature on our cover. Since its founding in 1980, the PMC has contributed well over $1 billion to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, a tremendous feat that continues to grow. This year alone the PMC raised a record-breaking $78 million with 100% of rider-raised funds going to Dana-Farber. The compassion and determination of PMC riders inspire us all, and their commitment to defying cancer is a powerful reminder of what we can accomplish together.

Thanks to your support, we have built a strong foundation for advancing cancer research, treatment, and care for every patient who walks through our doors. As we look ahead, I am filled with hope for all that we will accomplish. I look forward to celebrating each new advance with you, knowing none of these achievements would be possible without your partnership.

With heartfelt appreciation,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer
Seven-year Pan-Mass Challenge rider

excerpt.rendered: As I reflect on this past year, I am filled with immense gratitude for the generosity and unwavering commitment of our Dana-Farber community. Your steadfast support has been a driving force behind so many of our achievements, and it is because of you that we have been able to navigate challenges and embrace new opportunities with hope and determination.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to the tenacity and generosity of our entire community over the last seven years of The Dana-Farber Campaign, we are defying cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: We are thrilled to unveil the Spring 2023 issue of Impact—the first of our newly redesigned magazine and website!

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One of the things that makes Dana-Farber such a special place is our emphasis on teamwork.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Dr. Sidney Farber achieved the first remissions in childhood leukemia in 1947, he changed everything.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When I first stepped into my role at Dana-Farber in 2019, I was immediately struck by the endless compassion and dedication of the people around me.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: September has arrived, and with it the end of summer and the close of another successful Jimmy Fund event season.

title.rendered: Defying Cancer 26.2 miles at a time

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Sofi Elbadawi
Photography by Justin Knight, Kelly Dillon Photography

On Monday, April 21, more than 500 runners completed the 129th Boston Marathon® as part of the 2025 Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge (DFMC) team. This year’s DFMC athletes collectively raised over $8.3 million and counting for the Claudia Adams Barr Program in Innovative Basic Cancer Research, which provides funding for groundbreaking ideas at their earliest stages, propelling them toward discovery and potential cures.

Among this year’s DFMC team members was Tara Kenney, a Boston native whose connection to the team was deeply personal. Running the Boston Marathon had always been a lifelong dream for Tara, but it never felt like an achievable goal. That all changed when her father was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme grade IV (GBM) in February 2024. “Seeing my father face his diagnosis with grace, strength, and humor inspired me to do something bigger than myself and to join the DFMC team in his honor,” she shared. Motivated by her father’s courage, Tara was able to accomplish her goal of completing the Boston Marathon, crossing the finish line in Copley Square with a photo of her father raised high.

For Tara, running the Boston Marathon with the DFMC team was not only a personal achievement, but also a testament to the power of community and shared purpose. “I feel so lucky to have met teammates who supported me through my marathon training, but also through the loss of my father,” she shared. “Over the course of the season, there is a bond that forms amongst teammates that can’t be described, and I feel so lucky to have been a part of it.”

Tara’s commitment to Dana-Farber’s mission is fueled by her father’s legacy. “Glioblastoma multiforme grade IV still does not have a cure,” she noted. “I want to continue supporting Dana-Farber Cancer Institute so that future patients and families facing this disease have options.”

Since its first steps in 1990, the DFMC team has directed 100% of funds raised—more than $140 million to date—to the Claudia Adams Barr Program in Innovative Basic Cancer Research. Anthony G. Letai, MD, PhD, a Claudia Adams Barr Program Investigator, emphasized the importance of basic science research. “The Claudia Adams Barr Program in Innovative Basic Cancer Research provides funds for new ideas going in new directions,” he explained. “It can be challenging to secure funding for new research directions through more traditional pathways. With so much uncertainty surrounding National Institutes of Health funding, the role of this program has never been more important.”

“Seeing my father face his diagnosis with grace, strength, and humor inspired me to do something bigger than myself.”

Tara Kenney, 2025 DFMC Runner

Support from the DFMC team has enabled researchers like Letai to explore innovative approaches that can lead to significant advancements in cancer treatment. “For me, it gave me the ability to go in a new direction at several points in my career,” he shared. “In one case, the eventual impact was a new treatment for both acute myeloid leukemia and chronic lymphocytic
leukemia.”

Thanks to runners like Tara and researchers like Letai, the DFMC team is making strides in the fight against cancer, 26.2 miles at a time.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Science has long been the catalyst for transformative cancer care. More recently, we’ve witnessed revolutionary advances that have benefited patients and those who hold them dear.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge raises nearly $7 million in support of Claudia Adams Barr Program investigators
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge (DFMC) attracts runners from across the globe as they take on 26.2 miles in support of innovative basic research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute each year.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge accelerates basic cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Around mile 20 of the 2023 Boston Marathon,® Leah Meehan was in pain from a knee injury and struggling to keep pace. Out of nowhere, a bystander ran up to her with a bowl of bananas and said, “Take one of these. It will help you.”

img.alt_text: A Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge runner participating in the 2023 Boston Marathon

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber recruits largest B.A.A. Half Marathon® team to date
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2023 B.A.A. Half Marathon® was a race to remember, with 650 participants running Sunday, Nov. 12, to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s race toward a cancer-free future.

img.alt_text: A group photo of Dana-Farber runners at the BAA Half Marathon in 2023

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sheer joy and “finding the fun”: DFMC runners defy cancer with $8.8 million raised
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge runners raised $8.8 million in 2024 to benefit the Claudia Adams Barr Program in Innovative Basic Cancer Research, advancing promising ideas at their earliest stages so they can move forward toward discovery and cure.

img.alt_text: George O’Malley, who has run twelve marathons for DFMC, holds hands with friends after the race

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back on course with the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 34 years, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporters have come together for a day of inspiration and hope at the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, raising lifesaving funds to defy cancer for patients everywhere.

img.alt_text: Walkers and volunteers on the route of the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk

title.rendered: Impactful Progress: President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, reflects on his first year and strategic vision for the future of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Hannah White Hannah

As Dana-Farber Cancer Institute marks a transformative year under the leadership of President and CEO and Susan Smith Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, Impact spoke with him about the significant milestones achieved and the exciting path ahead.

Ebert stepped into his new leadership role at a pivotal moment for Dana-Farber, with plans for a new inpatient cancer hospital, major ambulatory expansion, and a rising demand for cancer care while the Institute simultaneously faced changes in federal research funding. Reflecting on his first year, Ebert shared insights into leading during a time of uncertainty. “It’s been an incredible privilege,” he remarked. “I’m proud of our agility in responding to changes in our external environment while maintaining our culture and our sense of mission.”

Soon after assuming his role, Ebert initiated an Institute-wide strategic planning process. Illustrating a commitment to maintaining culture throughout the organization, the strategic planning process engaged faculty and staff across Dana-Farber for their input to develop the plan for the future of the Institute. Ebert focused on the “big three” pillars—research, clinical, and education—as foundational to Dana-Farber’s future, specifically reaffirming Dana-Farber’s equal commitment to cancer research and clinical care while increasing the emphasis on education at all levels.

“I’m proud of our agility in responding to changes in our external environment while maintaining our culture and our sense of mission.”

Benjamin L. Ebert

Looking to the future, Ebert is focused on how to provide the best possible environment for basic, translational, and clinical research. He noted that artificial intelligence is poised to reshape oncology research, driving advancements from basic science to clinical trials. Ebert emphasized the potential of AI in transforming Dana-Farber’s future: “Our investment into artificial intelligence will influence diverse types of research and the future of clinical oncology.”

Clinically, a central component of Ebert’s strategic growth plan is the development of a new state-of-the-art cancer hospital in collaboration with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. This facility will integrate inpatient and ambulatory care, enhancing patient experiences and improving outcomes. Additionally, improving care for our pediatric oncology patients includes a proposed proton therapy facility and further developing our collaboration with Boston Children’s Hospital.

Recognizing the importance of knowledge in driving innovation, Ebert also stressed that Dana-Farber is committed to expanding its educational initiatives. “A major part of the strategic plan is expanding our education efforts,” he explained. This initiative aims to enhance educational materials for our patients and opportunities to train future oncology healthcare professionals, positioning Dana-Farber as a leading source of cancer knowledge.

Ebert emphasized that philanthropy plays a crucial role in each of Dana-Farber’s initiatives, providing us with ongoing support for our greatest priorities. “Philanthropy enables us to accomplish ambitious research objectives and deliver compassionate care. Our donor community is vital for transforming our institution,” said Ebert. Now more than ever, the support of donors is essential for realizing the vision of the new cancer hospital and advancing groundbreaking research.

Ebert is clear that accessible cancer care remains at the heart of Dana-Farber’s mission: From building a network of clinics across Massachusetts and New England, to mammogram vans that offer screenings in communities that otherwise may not have immediate access to Dana-Farber-level care. “We are expanding our network of clinics and working with community partners to improve coordination of care,” said Ebert.

As Ebert looks ahead to his second year, he is excited about defining cancer care for years to come with the Future Cancer Hospital, advancing research, and expanding educational efforts. “The opportunities ahead are greater than ever, and it’s incredibly motivating to be part of this transformative journey.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phyllis and Richard Krock
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

jetpack-related-posts.title: A new chapter in Dana-Farber leadership
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On October 1, 2024, Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, was succeeded by Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, as President and CEO of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: NYC reception spotlights future of research and care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Trustees, Pan-Mass Challenge Heavy Hitters, supporters, and friends gathered at Cure in New York City to meet Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, and engage in conversation about the path forward for Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Three people speaking at an event on stage

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lubins honored with Dana-Farber’s highest award for transformative impact
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Richard and Nancy Lubin received the 2024 Sidney Farber Medical Research Award for their visionary philanthropy and unwavering commitment to cancer science and care.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD; President Emerita Laurie H. Glimcher, MD; and Nancy and Richard Lubin at the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award presentation

jetpack-related-posts.title: Van Allen named to Chandra Nohria Family Chair for AI in Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This endowed chair is the first in the field of artificial intelligence to be established at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: Nitin Nohria; Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD; Monica Chandra; and Eliezer Van Allen, MD

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber faculty are part of “grand challenge” to defeat childhood tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has been awarded more than $3 million in funding as part of a Cancer Grand Challenge to find new treatments for solid tumors in children.

title.rendered: Conquering blood cancers is focus of Blood Cancer United grants

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

Each year, nearly 200,000 Americans are diagnosed with leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, or another bloodborne cancer. Blood Cancer United has awarded $4.2 million in grants to eight Dana-Farber physician-scientists working to better understand, treat, and potentially cure these often deadly diseases.

Andrew Lane, MD, PhD, and Anthony Letai, MD, PhD, received the organization’s prestigious multiyear Discovery Grants, which support groundbreaking research of blood cancers’ properties and vulnerabilities to advance treatments for them.

Lane, associate chief of the Division of Hematologic Neoplasia, is exploring how existing drugs that block the PI3 kinase gamma pathway in solid tumors could benefit certain patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML).

Letai’s work focuses on improving the performance of CAR T cells—natural immune cells that are genetically modified to recognize and attack the proteins on the surface of cancer cells—against blood cancers. While CAR T cells have produced lifesaving results in some cases, their effectiveness is limited by how long they survive in the body.

Blood Cancer United, in collaboration with the Follicular Lymphoma Foundation and the Institute for Follicular Lymphoma Innovation, also awarded grants to Philippe Armand, MD, PhD, and Mark Murakami, MD. Armand is the chief of the Lymphoma Division and the Harold and Virginia Lash Endowed Chair in Lymphoma Research at Dana-Farber.

Follicular lymphoma (FL) is an often incurable type of indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma. It is typically managed through a combination of chemotherapy and immunotherapy that can have detrimental side effects and negatively impact quality of life.

Armand and co-principal investigator Reid Merryman, MD, are conducting a phase two clinical trial of a chemotherapy-free regimen based on bispecific antibodies in patients with previously untreated FL. If successful, the trial could pave the way for a new, effective, and chemotherapy-free frontline treatment option for FL patients. Murakami is focused on understanding how some lymphoma cells survive this treatment and go on to cause relapse, with the goal of selecting patients for this type of therapy and ultimately devising improved future treatments.

Other Blood Cancer United grantees are Rizwan Romee, MD (Clinical Trials), Reina Takeda, MD, PhD, and Nicoletta Cieri, MD, PhD (Special Fellows), and Rachel Mersfelder, a medical student studying with the David G. Nathan, MD, Professor of Pediatrics at Harvard Medical School Kimberly Stegmaier, MD [Student Mentorship and Research Training (SMART)].

“Research is the key to unlocking the complexities of blood cancers, and we look forward with great anticipation to the results of these Dana-Farber studies and their positive impact on quality of life for blood cancer patients and their families,” said E. Anders Kolb, MD, Blood Cancer United’s president and CEO.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society attacks rare and resistant blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS) has awarded six grants totaling $5.8 million to Dana-Farber investigators.

img.alt_text: An artist’s rendering of bone marrow cells showing acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: IMS grants drive innovative multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Myeloma Society (IMS) recently awarded three Dana-Farber scientists grants totaling $525,000 to promote research on the blood cancer multiple myeloma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon invests in promising early career scientists
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded more than $3.2 million in grants to nine early career investigators at Dana-Farber, including Mounica Vallurupalli, MD, who was named the foundation’s first Damon Runyon-David M. Livingston, MD, Physician-Scientist.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon supports bold research by emerging talent
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded $1.22 million in grants to four early career investigators at Dana-Farber whose research has the potential to yield important breakthroughs in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Radical collaborations target intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: BTC has awarded $22.9 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers working across multiple institutions to unlock the secrets of four difficult-to-treat cancers and intercept or develop cutting-edge treatments for them.

title.rendered: Dana-Farber faculty are part of “grand challenge” to defeat childhood tumors

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

Dana-Farber has been awarded more than $3 million in funding as part of a Cancer Grand Challenge to find new treatments for solid tumors in children. “Outcomes for some pediatric cancers have not improved in more than 30 years,” said David Scott, PhD, director of Cancer Grand Challenges.

“Standard treatment regimens continue to rely on cytotoxic agents and, often, radiotherapy, which induce an alarming rate of severe health effects later in life.”

In 2025, about 15,000 U.S. children and adolescents ages birth to 19 are expected to be diagnosed with cancer, according to the American Cancer Society. Solid tumors, which include brain tumors, neuroblastoma, and others, make up a significant portion of these cases.

The Dana-Farber faculty members working on the Grand Challenge are part of a collaborative, international team called PROTECT—Harnessing PROTEin Degradation for Advanced Childhood Tumors. Protein degraders are an emerging class of therapeutic agents designed to target and eliminate specific proteins within cancer cells. Kimberly Stegmaier, MD, is leading the Dana-Farber contingent, which includes Scott Armstrong, MD, PhD, the Ted Williams Chair at Dana-Farber; Cigall Kadoch, PhD, the Meredith and Billy Starr Investigator at Dana-Farber; Eric Fischer, PhD, the Joseph Deitch Family Chair at Dana-Farber; and Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, the Richard and Susan Smith Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School. Stegmair is the David G. Nathan, MD, Professor of Pediatrics at Harvard Medical School as well as chair of the Pediatric Oncology Department. Team PROTECT is led by Stefan Pfister, MD, from the German Cancer Research Center/DKFZ in Germany, uniting clinicians, advocates, and scientists across 10 institutions and five countries.

“Cures will require innovative interventions that specifically target the unique biology of pediatric tumors,” Stegmaier said. “Our goal is to develop a new generation of therapeutic approaches for children with Ewing sarcoma, neuroblastoma, synovial sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, ependymoma, and high-grade glioma by targeting proteins previously thought to be undruggable.”

The team is developing small molecule prototype drugs that work by bringing together proteins expressed in the cancer cells and a special enzyme called an E3 ligase. This enzyme targets the protein for destruction, allowing the cell to dispose of it.

The goal is to advance the most promising project to the point where an Investigational New Drug (IND) application can be filed with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, demonstrating that a drug is reasonably safe for initial testing in humans. If the IND application is approved, Phase 1 clinical trials can begin.

Cancer Grand Challenges is a global research initiative that identifies the toughest challenges in cancer research. Team PROTECT is funded by Cancer Research UK, the National Cancer Institute, The Spanish Association Against Cancer, and KiKa (Children Cancer Free Foundation).

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor has awarded three grants totaling $850,000 to advance metastatic breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation continues steadfast support
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The legacy of a remarkable little girl has guided the mission of Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation (ALSF) since it was established in 2005.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer funds groundbreaking Dana-Farber pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer has awarded two grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to support groundbreaking pediatric cancer research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ben and Catherine Ivy Foundation helps advance glioblastoma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Ben and Catherine Ivy Foundation has awarded $524,081 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to advance novel immunotherapy approaches to treat glioblastoma.

title.rendered: Smith Family support inspires others to help speed multiple myeloma research

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Brittany Flaherty
Photography by Sam Ogden

Dana-Farber is a global leader in developing new treatments to help patients with multiple myeloma (MM), having played a critical role in developing and testing nearly all of the 19 new lifesaving MM therapies approved since 2003. Thanks to these advances, MM patients now live three- to five-times longer than they did two decades ago. Unfortunately, some MM disease subtypes do not respond to existing treatments, and many patients who respond initially develop resistance to these drugs over time. Because of this, MM continues to exact a heavy toll, claiming the lives of more than 100,000 people worldwide each year.

At Dana-Farber, Paul Richardson, MD, director of clinical research at the Jerome Lipper Multiple Myeloma Center, is poised to address the urgent needs of these patients. Richardson and his team are internationally renowned for spearheading clinical trials that elevate the standard of MM care, bringing new hope to patients with difficult forms of the disease. Philanthropy is critical to their efforts, and Richardson has found an important partner in Robert and Dana Smith, who recently made a $3 million gift to continue supporting his advanced clinical trials research. This gift builds on the Smiths’ past support of Richardson’s clinical trials work, which inspired a remarkable four-fold increase in donor commitments to MM clinical research from other supporters. This collective philanthropy helped Richardson expand his team by 46% in 4 years, which in turn led to an 18.5% increase in active MM trials from 2020 to 2024.

“This advanced clinical trials program is the tip of the spear in addressing the most vexing challenges in multiple myeloma.”

Robert Smith

“Our team is determined to develop and refine new therapies and treatment strategies for patients with the most challenging forms of multiple myeloma to further improve outcomes,” said Richardson. “We are profoundly grateful that Rob and Dana have partnered with us toward this goal, and for the entire community that they inspire to support our crucial efforts to help patients and our overall mission to turn the tide on myeloma.”

Expanded clinical trials have helped expedite the delivery of new MM drugs to patients at an unprecedented pace, as evidenced by FDA approval for eight new MM therapies since 2020. Continued support will help Richardson sustain and expand this robust portfolio of clinical trials, expediting his team’s ability to find the next breakthrough treatments.

“This advanced clinical trials program is the tip of the spear in addressing the most vexing challenges in multiple myeloma,” said Robert.

“Translating basic discoveries into more therapeutic options that can improve patient quality of life is precisely where targeted philanthropy can unlock the future of living with, and ultimately curing, this disease. Paul and his impressive team have the breadth of talent, creativity, and the unstoppable will to build on their impressive body of work. These are dollars well spent!”
